guard: a remote conversation renames only on an authoritative collision of a valid name, an unauthenticated, missing or foreign call runs nothing, each call runs on its own connection's configuration, and the gateway offers and reports only its remote tool subset, and its own request handler serves POST as stateless JSON with the caller's authentication and refuses every other method
why: A hosted MCP client pools one bearer and one MCP session across conversations, so the
connection_id is the only thing that keeps one conversation's words under its own identity.

mutations.name: the handler serves every method
mutations.expectRed: GET answers 405 with no stream to open
mutations.cell: GET answers 405 with no stream to open
mutations.note: A stateless GET would then open an event stream that never carries a message and stays open until the client leaves.

mutations.name: the handler drops the caller's authentication
mutations.expectRed: the requested name is used when free
mutations.cell: the requested name is used when free
mutations.note: Every tool would then see no authentication and refuse, so no conversation could connect.

mutations.name: the handler answers POST as an event stream
mutations.expectRed: a POST is answered as one JSON response
mutations.cell: a POST is answered as one JSON response
mutations.note: A buffering proxy in front of the endpoint could then hold a response it cannot tell is complete.

mutations.name: the handler sends no default instructions
mutations.expectRed: the handler sends the default instructions
mutations.cell: the handler sends the default instructions
mutations.note: A client would then get no instruction to connect once per conversation and keep its connection_id.
